entries.definition: Measure an ingredient by mass, volume or count and add it to a target.
Move food or a vessel's contents from one place to another.
Rinse ingredients under water until clean (or water runs clear for rice/legumes).
Leave an ingredient in liquid for a time.

entries.definition: Separate solids from liquid using a strainer or lid.
Remove skin or shell.
Remove stems, seeds, fat, bones or inedible parts.
Crack eggs into a target, checking for shell fragments.
Cut to a shape and size (dice, slice, julienne, mince, chop...).
Grate on a grater or microplane.
Crush with a mortar, press or masher.
Combine ingredients until evenly distributed.
Whisk to incorporate air or to a stage (soft/stiff peaks).
Gently fold to keep air in.
Knead dough until smooth and elastic.
Blend in a blender or food processor to a texture.
Combine fat and liquid into a stable emulsion.
Coat with marinade or seasoning and rest (refrigerate if perishable).

entries.definition: Add seasoning; optionally taste and adjust.
Shape into balls, patties, logs, sheets or other forms.
Roll dough to a thickness.
Fill vegetables, pastry or leaves; or wrap filling.
Assemble components in layers or a set arrangement.
Make wells in a sauce, dough or flour mound.
Bring a vessel, oven, oil or liquid to a target temperature.

tempC.description: Target temperature of the envelope medium. Must lie within envelope.tempC.

envelope.note: Two-stage cooling: from 60 °C to 21 °C within 2 h, then to 5 °C within 4 more hours. Large batches are a critical control point.

tempC.description: Target temperature of the envelope medium. Must lie within envelope.tempC.

envelope.note: Hot holding at or above 60 °C (WHO Five Keys). Below 60 °C for more than 2 h counts as time out of temperature control.

entries.definition: Add garnish.
Portion and arrange on plates.
Hand over for eating within a time window, optionally kept hot/cold.
Wait for a duration or external event (no action on food).
Run extraction (hood) at a level.
Clean tools/surfaces (allergen cross-contact control).

A step imported from a human recipe that has not been classified into an executable operation. Carries the original sentence and an optional opHint. No device declares this capability, so a dry run assigns it to a person or refuses; it never executes on a machine (RFC-0009).
